subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-safe by default, or should `deleteAfterRun` remain a one-shot-only lifecycle contract?
rationale: This PR and the open strict-validation PR encode opposite product contracts, and the choice affects existing persisted cron jobs, session retention, and operator upgrade behavior.

options.title: Complete recurring cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require a persisted-row or doctor/load path for existing omitted jobs while preserving explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

options.title: Reject recurring delete-after-run
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation direction after documenting a compatible recovery path for affected users.

options.title: Accept fresh-create only
options.body: Land the new default only for newly created jobs and explicitly document that existing omitted recurring isolated jobs require operator action or a later migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require a persisted-row or doctor/load path for existing omitted jobs while preserving explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice spans cron store migration/default semantics and product compatibility, and steipete has recent history in that store boundary.
